name: Jemima
title: Job's eldest daughter after the restoration
summary: Jemima was the oldest of the three daughters born to Job after God restored his wealth and health. She and her sisters were known as the most beautiful women in all the land, and they received an inheritance along with their brothers, which was very unusual for that time.

keyEvents.title: Job's restoration
keyEvents.description: After Job had endured his trials and God restored his wealth, he was blessed with ten new children, including Jemima as the eldest daughter.

keyEvents.title: The naming of Jemima
keyEvents.description: Job named his eldest daughter Jemima, which means 'dove' or 'daylight,' a symbol of peace and new hope after suffering.

keyEvents.title: Known for her beauty
keyEvents.description: Jemima and her sisters Kesia and Keren-Happuk were described as the most beautiful women in all the land, highlighting God's rich blessing upon Job.

keyEvents.title: Inheritance among brothers
keyEvents.description: Job gave Jemima and her sisters an inheritance along with their brothers, a very unusual and progressive step that demonstrated Job's generosity and justice.

keyEvents.title: Part of Job's double blessing
keyEvents.description: Jemima's birth was part of the double blessing that Job received from God after his faithfulness through suffering. Job lived another 140 years and saw four generations of his descendants.
